title: Standardised treatment contrasts with estimate()
text: Given formula = Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2 (right-hand side lists confounders) treatment = "", estimate(): fits working model Surv(time, status) ~ * (x1 + x2) chosen learner, sets level every subject predicts Ŝ(t∣Xi,)\hat S(t \mid X_i, ), averages subjects get counterfactual mean curves S‾(t)=n−1∑̂(t∣Xi,)\bar S_a(t) = n^{-1} \sum_i \hat S(t \mid X_i, ), contrasts one

title: Standardised treatment contrasts with estimate()
text: estimate() plug-G-formula estimator. doubly robust carries protection outcome-model misspecification beyond treatment--confounder interactions adds automatically. estimate causal interpretation : consistency – observed outcome equals potential outcome treatment actually received; unmeasured confounding given covariates formula; positivity – treatment levels possible every covariate pattern; interference subjects; correctly specified outcome model. non-manipulable attribute (sex, biomarker), read result covariate-adjusted marginal contrast, effect.

title: Interpretable Survival Machine Learning Framework
text: Unified survival machine learning interpretability R. survalis provides unified framework survival machine learning R. supports 22 learners, evaluation metrics, cross-validation, benchmarking, model-agnostic interpretability methods common survival-probability matrix (survmat) interface. survalis available CRAN: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=survalis.

title: Interpretable Survival Machine Learning Framework
text: fit() / predict() / evaluate() / tune() / compare() / interpret() / estimate() cover whole workflow. granular fit_*() / predict_*() / compute_*() / benchmark*() functions remain available low-level layer; see vignette("-1.0", package = "survalis") ?"survalis-lowlevel".
code: library(survalis) f <- Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype  m   <- fit(f, veteran, model = "ranger", spec = list(num.trees = 500)) predict(m, veteran[1:5, ], times = c(90, 180, 365))          # survmat evaluate(m, times = c(90, 180, 365), resampling = cv(5))     # resampled metrics  cmp <- compare(f, veteran, models = c("coxph", "ranger", "densemlp"),                times = c(90, 180, 365)) plot(cmp)  plot(interpret(m, "shap", newdata = veteran[1, ], times = 180)) estimate(f, veteran, model = "ranger", treatment = "trt", tau = 365)

title: Interpretable Survival Machine Learning Framework
text: Version 1.1.0 adds set downstream tools work fitted models survmat predictions used throughout package: screen_fdr() performs univariate Cox screening Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control optional minimum-screen guarantee. estimate_rmst() plot_rmst() estimate standardized marginal RMST two-group RMST contrast percentile-bootstrap intervals. compute_shap_matrix() plot_shap_beeswarm() summarize time-integrated SHAP contributions across observations. roc_survmat() dca_survmat() provide IPCW time-dependent ROC decision-curve analyses, plot_roc() plot_dca() helpers.
code: # FDR screening selected <- screen_fdr(   Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + diagtime + prior,   data = veteran,   alpha = 0.1,   minscreen = 2 )  # Standardized RMST contrast between treatment groups rmst <- estimate_rmst(   mod_cox,   data = veteran,   tau = 200,   times = seq(10, 300, by = 10),   trt_col = "trt",   R = 200,   seed = 1 )  # Time-dependent ROC and decision curves from survmat predictions pred_100 <- predict_coxph(mod_cox, veteran, times = 100) roc <- roc_survmat(Surv(veteran$time, veteran$status), pred_100, t_star = 100) dca <- dca_survmat(Surv(veteran$time, veteran$status), pred_100, t_star = 100) plot_roc(roc) plot_dca(dca)

title: Interpretable Survival Machine Learning Framework
text: Seven verbs cover whole workflow: fit(), predict(), evaluate(), tune(), compare(), interpret(), estimate() Every learner returns standardized survalis_fit (mlsurv_model subclass) Matrix predictions return survmat: columns t=100, t=200, …, grid recorded attr(x, "times") Evaluation fully modular: learner id works evaluate()/compare() cv()/holdout()/group_cv()/bootstrap() resampling Designed interpretability post prediction, single interpret() entry point

title: Interpretable Survival Machine Learning Framework
text: 1. Fit model 2. Predict survival probabilities predict() also returns quantities via type: "risk" (1 - S(t)), "chf", "hazard", "rmst", "quantile", "median". 3. Evaluate model performance 4. Compare multiple learners compare() evaluates every learner resampling folds, results paired; tune = TRUE tunes tunable learner first.  5. Kaplan-Meier curves plot_survcurve() produces styled Kaplan-Meier curve confidence ribbon, log-rank p-value, aligned number--risk table, spirit survminer::ggsurvplot() implemented natively (dependency survminer).  6. Visualize interpretation interpret() single entry point every explanation method; plot() dispatches matching plot_*() helper.
code: mod_cox <- fit(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, veteran, model = "coxph") mod_cox #> <survalis_fit> model = coxph  (engine: survival) #>   formula: Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype #>   data:    137 obs, 128 events (93%) pred <- predict(mod_cox, newdata = veteran[1:5, ], times = c(100, 200)) pred #> <survmat> survival  |  5 obs x 2 times  [100, 200] #>          t=100     t=200 #> [1,] 0.6142681 0.3541697 #> [2,] 0.6944383 0.4599242 #> [3,] 0.5556797 0.2860796 #> [4,] 0.6033305 0.3408724 #> [5,] 0.6959633 0.4620783 ev <- evaluate(mod_cox, times = c(80, 160), resampling = cv(5, seed = 123)) ev #> <survalis_eval> model = coxph #> <survalis_resampling> 5-fold CV, strata = status, seed = 123 #>   grid: 2 times in [80, 160] #>   cindex  0.7180  (sd 0.0530, 95% [0.6720, 0.7640], n = 5) #>   ibs     0.1820  (sd 0.0420, 95% [0.1460, 0.2190], n = 5) summary(ev) #>   metric  mean    sd n    se lower upper #> 1 cindex 0.718 0.053 5 0.023 0.672 0.764 #> 2    ibs 0.182 0.042 5 0.019 0.146 0.219 cmp <- compare(   Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype,   data = veteran,   models = c("coxph", "rpart", "ranger"),   times = c(80, 160),   resampling = cv(3, seed = 1)   )  cmp #> <survalis_compare> 3 models #> <survalis_resampling> 3-fold CV, strata = status, seed = 1 #>  #>   cindex (higher is better): #>    * coxph            0.7307  (se 0.0188) #> 0.0042) #>      rpart            0.2160  (se 0.0062) plot(cmp) plot_survcurve(Surv(time, status) ~ trt, data = veteran) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_ribbon()`). shap_meanabs <- interpret(   mod_cox, "shap",   newdata     = veteran[100, ],   times       = 80,   sample.size = 50,   aggregate   = TRUE,   shap_method = "meanabs"   )  as.data.frame(shap_meanabs) #>           feature         phi #> trt           trt 0.000000000 #> celltype celltype 0.017380404 #> karno       karno 0.019501719 #> diagtime diagtime 0.000000000 #> age code: pdp_age <- interpret(mod_cox, "pdp", feature = "age", times = c(100, 200, 300))  plot(pdp_age, which = "per_time") plot(pdp_age, which = "integrated", smooth = TRUE) #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x' ale_karno <- interpret(mod_cox, "ale", feature = "karno", times = c(100, 200, 300))  plot(ale_karno, which = "per_time") plot(ale_karno, which = "integrated", smooth = TRUE) #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x' local_surrogate <- interpret(   mod_cox, "surrogate",   newdata     = veteran[1, , drop = FALSE],   times       = c(100, 200, 300),   target_time = 200,   k           = 5   )  as.data.frame(local_surrogate) #>    feature feature_value      effect target_time #> 1    karno            60 0.491034890         200 #> 2 celltype      squamous 0.189632633         200 #> 3      age            69 0.120729843         200 #> 4 diagtime             7 0.001800378         200 #> 5    prior             0 0.000000000         200 plot(local_surrogate, top_n = 10) tree_surrogate <- interpret(mod_cox, "tree_surrogate", times = c(100, 200, 300))  plot(tree_surrogate, type = "importance", top_n = 5) # plot(tree_surrogate, type = "tree") varimp_res <- interpret(   mod_cox, "varimp",   times          = c(100, 200, 300),   metric         = "ibs",   n_repetitions  = 5,   seed           = 123   )  as.data.frame(varimp_res) #> # basetable: 6 x 5 #>    feature importance importance_05 importance_95 scaled_importance #> 1    karno     0.0672        0.0494        0.0826         100.00000 #> 2 celltype     0.0468        0.0394        0.0574          69.64286 #> 3      age    -0.0022       -0.0030       -0.0012           3.27381 #> 4      trt     0.0000        0.0000        0.0000           0.00000 #> 5 diagtime     0.0000        0.0000        0.0000           0.00000 #> 6    prior     0.0000        0.0000        0.0000           0.00000 plot(varimp_res) interaction_1way <- interpret(mod_cox, "interaction", times = c(100, 200, 300),                               target_time = 200, type = "1way") interaction_heatmap <- interpret(mod_cox, "interaction", times = c(100, 200, 300),                                  target_time = 200, type = "heatmap") interaction_time <- interpret(mod_cox, "interaction", times = c(100, 200, 300),                               type = "time")  plot(interaction_1way, type = "1way") plot(interaction_heatmap, type = "heatmap") plot(interaction_time, type = "time") counterfactuals <- interpret(   mod_cox, "counterfactual",   newdata            = veteran[1, , drop = FALSE],   times              = c(100, 200, 300),   target_time        = 200,   features_to_change = c("age", "karno", "diagtime"),   cost_penalty       = 0.01   )  as.data.frame(counterfactuals) #>    feature original_value suggested_value survival_gain change_cost #> 1    karno             60         81.0202        0.2347     21.0202 #> 2 diagtime              7          7.0808        0.0000      0.0808 #> 3      age             69         69.1313        0.0003      0.1313 #>   penalized_gain #> 1         0.0245 #> 2        -0.0008 #> 3        -0.0010 interpret(mod_cox, "calibration", eval_time = 80, n_bins = 10, n_boot = 30) |> plot()

what: Time-Dependent AUC from a Survival-Probability Matrix — auc_survmat
title: Time-Dependent AUC from a Survival-Probability Matrix — auc_survmat
text: Computes cumulative/dynamic time-dependent AUC using predicted survival probabilities specified time point (last column t_star NULL), following Uno et al. (2007) / Heagerty Zheng (2005) estimator implemented timeROC package. Cases subjects observed event strictly t_star; controls subjects known survive beyond t_star. Subjects censored t_star handled IPCW weighting.

title: Time-Dependent AUC from a Survival-Probability Matrix — auc_survmat
code: auc_survmat(object, predicted, t_star = NULL)

title: Time-Dependent AUC from a Survival-Probability Matrix — auc_survmat
text: object Surv object length \(n\). predicted n x k matrix data frame survival probabilities columns named "t=<time>". t_star Optional numeric time evaluate AUC; omitted, rightmost column predicted used.

title: Time-Dependent AUC from a Survival-Probability Matrix — auc_survmat
text: named numeric scalar: "auc".

title: Time-Dependent AUC from a Survival-Probability Matrix — auc_survmat
text: Risk scores defined 1 - S(t) chosen time. AUC computed case-control pairs using inverse-probability--censoring weights cases partial credit (0.5) ties.

title: Time-Dependent AUC from a Survival-Probability Matrix — auc_survmat
code: y <- survival::Surv(time = veteran$time, event = veteran$status) sp <- matrix(   stats::plogis(scale(veteran$karno)),   ncol = 1,   dimnames = list(NULL, "t=100") ) auc_survmat(y, predicted = sp, t_star = 100) #>      auc  #> 0.795944

title: Benchmark Survival Learners (Meta Function) — benchmark
text: single entry point comparing multiple survival learners. tune = FALSE (default), learner run fixed hyperparameters via benchmark_default_survlearners. tune = TRUE, learner tuned internally per outer fold via nested cross-validation using benchmark_tuned_survlearners.

title: Benchmark Survival Learners (Meta Function) — benchmark
code: benchmark(   formula,   data,   learners,   times,   metrics = c("cindex", "ibs"),   tune = FALSE,   folds = 5,   outer_folds = 5,   inner_folds = 5,   seed = 123,   ncores = 1,   inner_ncores = 1,   learner_args = list(),   refit_final = FALSE,   verbose = FALSE,   suppress_errors = TRUE,   ... )

what: Compute Feature Interactions for Survival Predictions — compute_interactions
title: Compute Feature Interactions for Survival Predictions — compute_interactions
text: Estimates global time-varying interaction strengths model predictions, using Friedman-H style decomposition adapted survival partial dependence. Works mlsurv_model matching predict_*() method returning survival probabilities.

title: Compute Feature Interactions for Survival Predictions — compute_interactions
code: compute_interactions(   model,   data,   times,   target_time = NULL,   features = NULL,   type = c("1way", "heatmap", "time"),   grid.size = 30,   batch.size = 100 )

title: Compute Feature Interactions for Survival Predictions — compute_interactions
text: model mlsurv_model created via fit_*() function; must include valid learner appropriate predict_<learner>() can dispatched. data Data frame used probe model (typically training data). times Numeric vector evaluation times used prediction. target_time Single time quantify interactions type = "1way" type = "heatmap". Required types. features Optional character vector feature names evaluate. Defaults predictors data except outcome columns. type One : "1way" – per-feature Friedman-H interaction strength vs. others target_time; "heatmap" – pairwise feature interaction matrix target_time; "time" – per-feature interaction strength across times. grid.size Integer; number random grid values / replicates used Monte Carlo marginalization (default 30). batch.size Reserved future batching support (currently unused).

title: Compute Feature Interactions for Survival Predictions — compute_interactions
text: data frame whose structure depends type: "1way": columns feature, interaction. "heatmap": columns feature1, feature2, interaction (symmetric zeros diagonal). "time": columns feature, time, interaction.

title: Compute Feature Interactions for Survival Predictions — compute_interactions
text: target time \(t^{*}\), let \(f(x)\) predicted survival probability. feature \(j\), approximate decomposition: $$ f(x) \approx f_j(x_j) + f_{-j}(x_{-j}) $$ Monte Carlo marginalization subsets features using random sampling empirical distribution data. reported interaction strength : $$ H_j(t^{*}) = \sqrt{ \frac{\sum ( f(x) - \{ \tilde f_j(x_j) + \tilde f_{-j}(x_{-j}) \})^2 }{ \sum f(x)^2 } } , $$ clipped [0, 1]. Pairwise heatmaps computed analogously \((j, k)\). Larger values indicate stronger non-additivity (interaction) involving feature(s). "time" mode repeats computation across times show dynamics.

title: Compute Feature Interactions for Survival Predictions — compute_interactions
text: Friedman, J. H., Popescu, B. E. (2008). Predictive learning via rule ensembles. Annals Applied Statistics. (Friedman's \(H\) interaction measure.)

title: Compute Feature Interactions for Survival Predictions — compute_interactions
code: mod <- fit_coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + trt, data = veteran) times <- c(80, 160) compute_interactions(   model = mod,   data = veteran,   times = times,   target_time = 80,   features = c("age", "karno"),   type = "1way",   grid.size = 6 ) #>   feature interaction #> 1     age   0.8789678 #> 2   karno   1.0000000

title: Time-Integrated SHAP Values for a Set of Observations — compute_shap_matrix
text: observation \(x\), per-time Shapley values \(\varphi_j(x, t)\) (compute_shap) time-integrated via trapezoidal rule requested time grid, $$   \Phi_j(x) = \int_0^{T} \varphi_j(x, t)\, dt   \approx \sum_{k=2}^{m} \frac{\varphi_j(x, t_k) + \varphi_j(x, t_{k-1})}{2}   (t_k - t_{k-1}), $$ using integration already implemented compute_shap(..., aggregate = TRUE, method = "integral"). produces one summary contribution per (observation, feature) reflects impact entire prediction horizon single value, plot_shap_beeswarm visualizes – opposed per-timepoint SurvSHAP(t) panel.

Default seq(0.01, 0.99, = 0.01). x dca_survmat object. title Plot title. missing, automatically generated title used. Pass NULL omit title entirely. ... Additional arguments passed plot.dca_survmat.

title: Decision Curve Analysis for Right-Censored Survival Outcomes — dca_survmat
text: predicted risk horizon \(\pi_i = 1 - \hat S(t^\star \mid X_i)\). threshold pt, subjects \(\pi_i \ge pt\) classified high-risk. Using IPCW identity Kaplan-Meier estimator (Graf et al. 1999), true- false-positive fractions estimated $$   \widehat{\mathrm{TPF}}(pt) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{=1}^n     (\pi_i \ge pt)\, \frac{\Delta_i\, (\tilde T_i \le t^\star)}{\hat G(\tilde T_i)},   \qquad   \widehat{\mathrm{FPF}}(pt) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{=1}^n     (\pi_i \ge pt)\, \frac{(\tilde T_i > t^\star)}{\hat G(t^\star)}, $$ net benefit $$   \widehat{\mathrm{NB}}(pt) = \widehat{\mathrm{TPF}}(pt) -     \widehat{\mathrm{FPF}}(pt) \cdot \frac{pt}{1-pt}. $$ "Treat " (classify everyone high-risk) reduces marginal IPCW-KM identity \(1 - \hat S_{\mathrm{KM}}(t^\star)\) TPF term \(\hat S_{\mathrm{KM}}(t^\star)\) FPF term. "Treat none" net benefit \(0\) definition.

title: Decision Curve Analysis for Right-Censored Survival Outcomes — dca_survmat
text: Vickers AJ, Elkin EB (2006). "Decision Curve Analysis: Novel Method Evaluating Prediction Models." Medical Decision Making, 26(6), 565-574. Vickers AJ, Van Calster B, Steyerberg EW (2019). "Simple, Step--Step Guide Interpreting Decision Curve Analysis." Diagnostic Prognostic Research, 3, 18. Graf E, Schmoor C, Sauerbrei W, Schumacher M (1999). "Assessment Comparison Prognostic Classification Schemes Survival Data." Statistics Medicine, 18(17-18), 2529-2545.

title: Fit a Bagged Nearest-Neighbour Survival Model — fit_bnnsurv
text: base learner \(b = 1, \dots, B\) draws bootstrap (subsample) training rows , optionally, random subset predictors. new observation \(x\), learner finds \(k\) training rows closest \(x\) returns weighted Kaplan-Meier curve $$\hat S_b(t \mid x) = \prod_{t_j \le t}   \left(1 - \frac{\sum_i w_i \delta_i 1\{T_i = t_j\}}                  {\sum_i w_i 1\{T_i \ge t_j\}}\right),$$ weights \(w_i = w(d(x, x_i))\). ensemble prediction average \(\hat S(t \mid x) = B^{-1} \sum_b \hat S_b(t \mid x)\), non-increasing step function \(t\). Training rows tied \(k\)-th nearest distance share remaining neighbour slots equally, predictions depend row order data. Mahalanobis distance uses covariance \(\Sigma_b\) base learner's sample: \(d(x, y)^2 = (x - y)^\top \Sigma_b^{+} (x - y)\), \(\Sigma_b^{+}\) Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse. Constant collinear columns (example dummy never varies bootstrap sample) therefore contribute nothing instead breaking inversion. metric = "euclidean" uses Euclidean distance standardized columns. Differences bnnSurvival: factors one-hot encoded (coded integer labels) new data reuse training levels; feature subsets drawn predictors (factor counts one predictor); constant columns detected variances; prediction runs current process (forking); predictions arbitrary times read step function rather linearly interpolated. numeric predictors, predictors per learner, constant weights tied distances, two engines give curves seed.

title: Fit a Stacked Survival Meta‑Learner (Time‑Varying NNLS) — fit_survmetalearner
text: Learns nonnegative, time‑specific stacking weights set base survival learners solving nonnegative least squares (NNLS) problem requested time \(t^{*}\). \(t^{*}\), target indicator \(Y = (T > t^{*})\); features base learners' predicted survival probabilities \(S_\ell(t^{*} \mid x)\). Weights constrained nonnegative normalized sum 1 per time point.

NULL (default), base learners learners fitted formula data, base_preds --fold predictions. time Numeric vector observed event/censoring times (length n). text: t times, function fits $$\min_{w \ge 0} \\mid Y - S w \|_2^2 \quad \text{s.t.} \ \sum_j w_j = 1$$ \(Y = (T > t)\) \(S\) matrix base survival probabilities \(t\). NNLS solution nnls renormalized sum 1 (solution zeros, weights remain NA time).

title: Fit a Stacked Survival Meta‑Learner (Time‑Varying NNLS) — fit_survmetalearner
code: form <- Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + trt times <- c(80, 160) mod_cox <- fit_coxph(form, data = veteran) mod_rpart <- fit_rpart(form, data = veteran) base_models <- list(coxph = mod_cox, rpart = mod_rpart) base_preds <- list(   coxph = predict_coxph(mod_cox, newdata = veteran, times = times),   rpart = predict_rpart(mod_rpart, newdata = veteran, times = times) ) meta_model <- fit_survmetalearner(   base_preds = base_preds,   time = veteran$time,   status = veteran$status,   times = times,   base_models = base_models,   formula = form,   data = veteran ) meta_model$weights #>            t=80 t=160 #> coxph 0.6630347     0 #> rpart 0.3369653     1

title: Fit a Survival Support Vector Machine — fit_survsvm
text: model accelerated failure time model \(\log T = f(x) + \varepsilon\) \(f(x) = \sum_i \beta_i k(x, x_i) + b\) reproducing kernel Hilbert space kernel \(k\). \(y_i = \log T_i\), \(f\) minimizes $$\frac12 \|f\|_k^2 + \frac{\gamma}{2} \sum_{:\,\delta_i = 1} (y_i - f(x_i))^2   + \frac{\gamma}{2} \sum_{:\,\delta_i = 0} \max(0,\, y_i - f(x_i))^2 ,$$ survival support vector regression Shivaswamy et al. (2007) Van Belle et al. (2011) squared losses: event time fitted sides, censored time penalized prediction falls . problem strictly convex piecewise quadratic, solved exactly active-set Newton method (Chapelle, 2007). Given active set \(\) (events, censored points predicted early), optimum solves least-squares SVM system $$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1^\top \\ 1 & K_{AA} + /\gamma \end{pmatrix}   \begin{pmatrix} b \\ \beta_A \end{pmatrix} =   \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ y_A \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \beta_{^c} = 0,$$ one Cholesky factorization; \(\) updated, line search, longer changes. quadratic programming solver involved. Censored points outside \(\) \(\beta_i = 0\) stored. Survival curves follow AFT form: \(S(t \mid x) = S_\varepsilon(\log t - f(x))\), \(S_\varepsilon\) Kaplan-Meier estimate cross-fitted residuals \(y_i - f_{-k()}(x_i)\): residual comes model fitted without observation's fold, curves made overconfident -sample fit. See predict_survsvm alternatives.

title: Fit a Survival Support Vector Machine — fit_survsvm
text: "add_kernel" Clinical (additive) kernel Daemen et al. (2012): average predictors \(\max(0, 1 - |x_j - z_j| / r_j)\) numeric ordered predictors (\(r_j\) training range) \(1\{x_j = z_j\}\) unordered factors. Scale free, positive semi-definite, factor counts one predictor. Constant predictors add constant. "lin_kernel" \(x^\top z / p\) standardized columns (factors treatment coding). "rbf_kernel" \(\exp(-\|x - z\|^2 / (2 \sigma^2))\) standardized columns; kernel.pars \(\sigma^2\), default number columns \(p\). "poly_kernel" \((x^\top z / p + c)^d\) standardized columns; kernel.pars \((c, d)\), default \((1, 2)\).

Sensitivity specificity swept every observed risk-score value \(c\): $$   \widehat{\mathrm{Se}}(c) = \frac{\sum_{\\text{cases}} w_i\, (\text{risk}_i \ge c)}   {\sum_{\\text{cases}} w_i}, \qquad   \widehat{\mathrm{Sp}}(c) = \frac{\sum_{\\text{controls}} (\text{risk}_i < c)}   {|\text{controls}|}. $$

what: FDR-Based Variable Screening via Univariate Cox Models — screen_fdr
title: FDR-Based Variable Screening via Univariate Cox Models — screen_fdr
text: Screens candidate covariates right-censored outcome fitting univariate Cox model \(\lambda(t \mid X_j) = \lambda_0(t)\exp(\beta_j X_j)\) per covariate, Wald-testing \(H_0: \beta_j = 0\), controlling false discovery rate (FDR) across tests via Benjamini-Hochberg (1995) step-procedure.

title: FDR-Based Variable Screening via Univariate Cox Models — screen_fdr
code: screen_fdr(formula, data, alpha = 0.1, minscreen = 5)

title: FDR-Based Variable Screening via Univariate Cox Models — screen_fdr
text: formula model formula Surv(time, status) outcome left-hand side candidate screening covariates right-hand side (used throughout survalis, e.g. fit_coxph). data data.frame containing variables formula. alpha Target FDR level (0, 1). Covariates BH-adjusted p-value (q-value) <= alpha retained. Default 0.1. minscreen Minimum number covariates retain. fewer minscreen covariates pass FDR threshold, smallest-p-value covariates added back minscreen reached (subject number candidate covariates available). Default 5.

title: FDR-Based Variable Screening via Univariate Cox Models — screen_fdr
text: character vector selected covariate names, attribute "screen_table" holding full data.frame feature, p_value, q_value, selected.

title: FDR-Based Variable Screening via Univariate Cox Models — screen_fdr
text: candidate covariate \(X_j\), survalis fits coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ X_j, data = data) extracts Wald p-value \(\beta_j\). Raw p-values \(p_1, \dots, p_p\) ordered \(p_{(1)} \le \cdots \le p_{(p)}\) BH-adjusted q-value \(k\)-th smallest p-value $$q_{(k)} = \min_{k \le l \le p} \left\{ \frac{p \cdot p_{(l)}}{l} \right\},$$ guaranteeing \(\mathrm{E}[\text{FDR}] \le \alpha\) retained set \(\{j : q_j \le \alpha\}\) (Benjamini Hochberg 1995).

title: FDR-Based Variable Screening via Univariate Cox Models — screen_fdr

title: Time-Dependent ROC/AUC Curve from a Survival-Probability Matrix — timeroc_survmat

title: survalis 1.7.0
text: granular functions (fit_*(), predict_*(), tune_*(), cv_survlearner(), score_survmodel(), benchmark*(), compute_*(), estimate_rmst(), …) longer scheduled removal. stay exported low-level layer verbs longer print one-time “granular survalis function” note. ?survalis-deprecated now ?survalis-lowlevel. fit() longer accepts engine arguments ...; pass spec = list(...). Extra arguments now give error instead warning. stpm2 learner removed: fit_stpm2() predict_stpm2() gone ‘rstpm2’ longer dependency. Use fit_rpsurv() / fit(model = "rpsurv"), fits Royston-Parmar model hazard, odds, probit scale adds nonlinear effects (nle). survsvm learner now engine longer depends ‘survivalsvm’. “quadprog” path called Matrix::nearPD(), stop “error code 1 Lapack routine ‘dsyevr’” depending BLAS/LAPACK library. new engine fits kernel survival support vector regression log time (squared loss events, one-sided squared loss censored times) solves exactly active-set Newton steps one Cholesky factorization , quadratic programming solver needed; 10 50 times faster. Survival curves now come Kaplan-Meier estimate cross-fitted residuals, S(t | x) = S_e(log t - f(x)), calibrated, instead exp(-t / f(x)), assumed exponential shape give negative times. dist = "lognormal" new; "exp" "weibull" remain available. clinical kernel ("add_kernel") treats factor one predictor accepts constant columns, "poly_kernel" fixed. type = "regression" supported (ranking types give survival curve); opt.meth diff.meth ignored. default gamma.mu now 0.1 tune_survsvm() grid c(0.01, 0.1, 1), matched new loss scale. fitted object’s engine now "survalis". bnnsurv learner (bagged k-nearest-neighbour Kaplan-Meier) now engine longer depends ‘bnnSurvival’, unmaintained. ‘bnnSurvival’ predicted parallel::mclapply(), forking session whose multithreaded BLAS (e.g. MKL) already running hang predict_bnnsurv(). new engine runs current process also: one-hot encodes factors (integer codes inside Mahalanobis distance) matches new data training levels; uses pseudo-inverse covariance, constant collinear columns bootstrap sample handled; draws feature subsets predictors (factor counts one); splits weight equally neighbours tied k-th distance, results longer depend row order; reads predictions arbitrary times step function instead interpolating linearly. numeric predictors default settings gives curves ‘bnnSurvival’ seed, ten times faster. metric = "euclidean" (standardized columns) new. fitted object’s engine now "survalis". survalis now declares R (>= 4.4.0) fastgbm (>= 0.7.0). claimed R 4.1, ‘fastgbm’ 0.6.1 needed R 4.5.0 ‘rms’ (imported ‘pec’) needs R 4.4.0, installation failed older R. survdnn learner removed, ‘survdnn’ ‘torch’ dependencies. ‘torch’ needs separate LibTorch download often failed install. Use densemlp learner (fit(..., model = "densemlp")), fits deep survival models native C++ backend. fit_survdnn(), predict_survdnn(), tune_survdnn() removed. survalis longer defines plot.formula() method. replaced graphics::plot.formula() every package soon survalis loaded (“Registered S3 method overwritten”). Use plot_survcurve() Kaplan-Meier curve.

title: survalis 1.6.4
text: Bug fixes found benchmarking every learner 31 survival datasets. fit_ranger() drops predictors constant data fitted . respect.unordered.factors = "order", ranger stopped “invalid type (NULL) variable ‘smry$strata’” factor single level, happens tuning folds data many rare binary predictors (metabric). fit_glmnet() predict_glmnet() accept single predictor. glmnet stops “x matrix 2 columns”, predictor matrix padded constant zero column. fit_aalen() standardizes numeric covariates predict_aalen() applies scaling. timereg::aalen() silently returned -zero fit covariates different scales, predicted survival 1 every subject. predict_flexsurvreg(), predict_bnnsurv(), predict_cforest() accept single evaluation time. one-time result now one-column matrix (one-row matrix, flat table flexsurvreg), single-time metrics brier ece can computed learners. fit_survmetalearner() can called formula data , benchmark() compare() . fits base learners (learners, default coxph, glmnet, rsf), builds --fold predictions, learns weights . predict_survmetalearner() interpolates weights requested times differ fitted grid. fit_xgboost() accepts max_depth eta. tune_xgboost() passed , every configuration failed silently tune() stopped unrelated “Unknown columns: ibs”. tune() stops clear message every configuration fails cross-validation. tune_survsvm() default param_grid, tune_survdnn() accepts default: argument check rejected default missing() always true . Errors raised inside parallel workers (ncores > 1) compare(), evaluate(), cv_survlearner() now reported. functionals::fmapn() returns try-error objects, dropped, failure surfaced object 'value' found.

title: survalis 1.6.0
text: Bug fix: survmat_to_rmst() (everything built : predict(type = "rmst"), estimate()) previously -integrated RMST -grid tau – restricted time grid times <= tau summed whole trapezoidal intervals , silently dropping fractional last interval instead interpolating . example, grid 0:5, tau = 3.5 returned value tau = 3 (wrong). RMST computation now delegated tvrmst::rmst_dynamic(), per-subject linear interpolation tau top cumulative trapezoidal curve. title: survalis 1.5.0

title: survalis 1.4.0
text: New learner: rpsurv (Royston-Parmar flexible parametric survival, via rpsurv package). fit_rpsurv()/predict_rpsurv() added (tuner), restricted cubic splines optional time-varying covariate effects (tve) choice scale (hazard/odds/normal). Registered list_survlearners(); 23 learners total.

title: survalis 1.3.0
text: fit(formula, data, model, spec, seed) – learner-agnostic fitting; returns survalis_fit (subclass mlsurv_model, every existing helper keeps working ). predict(fit, newdata, times, type) – type one "survival", "risk", "chf", "hazard" (returning validated survmat), "rmst", "quantile", "median" (numeric). evaluate(fit_or_formula, times, resampling, metrics) – resampled performance; survalis_fit reuses stored recipe. tune(formula, data, model, grid, resampling, metric) – grid search, returns refit best model survalis_fit. compare(formula, data, models, specs, resampling, metrics, tune) – paired multi-model leaderboard shared folds. interpret(fit, method, newdata, data, times, ...) – single entry point compute_* explanation methods, plot() dispatches paired helper. estimate(formula, data, model, estimand, treatment, tau) – standardised binary-treatment contrast G-computation, subject bootstrap (refit per replicate default) identification-assumptions note.

title: survalis 1.3.0
text: survmat prediction contract: n x length(times) numeric matrix carrying grid "times" attribute ("t=<time>" column names kept display legacy metric helpers) predicted quantity "quantity". Missing predictions non-increasing grids rejected. default_times(): recorded, data-dependent evaluation grid used whenever times omitted, runs stay reproducible. Resampling constructors cv() (repeats), holdout(), group_cv(), bootstrap(); reuse one spec across models paired comparisons.

title: survalis 1.1.0
text: Added screen_fdr(): univariate-Cox variable screening Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control, minscreen backfill guarantee. Added estimate_rmst() plot_rmst(): standardized RMST estimation via g-computation, percentile bootstrap inference. Dispatch marginal estimate two-arm causal-style contrast trt_col argument (NULL = marginal), matching plot_survmat()’s existing group dispatch convention rather separate function names. Added compute_shap_matrix() plot_shap_beeswarm(): beeswarm view SHAP contributions time-integrated full prediction horizon, built compute_shap()’s existing per-time Shapley decomposition. compute_shap() gained explicit features argument (defaulting setdiff(colnames(newdata), c(model$time, model$status))), replacing hardcoded c("time", "status", "event") exclusion, consistency compute_interactions()’s existing features argument. Added roc_survmat() (full time-dependent ROC curve, IPCW-weighted like auc_survmat()) dca_survmat() (decision curve analysis / net benefit right-censored outcomes, using Ĝ(t) IPCW estimator brier() auc_survmat()), plot()/plot_roc()/plot_dca() methods.
